cutoff_rationale: After the human had enumerated the exact edges in both directions and the zero-inbound property of every other SCC member. 5 min before activatedAt.
confirmed_concern: One package-level dependency cycle (a 6-member SCC) exists, and the root<->cli edge is the outermost, cheapest candidate to cut; the ownership question is which side should own the shared primitives the edge crosses.
investigation_findings: core-root -> cli is exactly 2 value edges, both static paths, confirmed by grep and by the package fan-in reading (fanIn = 2): one imports a driver control client into a session handler; the other imports a service-name vocabulary into the server entry — of which one imported symbol is entirely unused (a dead import).
cli -> core-root is the normal direction with 34 edges and is not itself a problem.
Every other SCC member (gate, gate/config, gate/factories, fan-in, primitives, kernel) contributes ZERO edges into cli.
Therefore removing those 2 edges leaves cli with no inbound edge from inside the cycle, so cli MUST leave the SCC.

The ownership reading: this is not CLI reaching backward into core, nor core wanting a CLI facade — two primitives genuinely shared by both layers were placed under cli/ only because their first historical consumer was CLI help text.
